body.en: Three-dimensional geometry and similarity ratios appear at the end of the EST II test, often combined with algebraic reasoning.

value.en: lengths \( k \) : areas \( k^2 \) : volumes \( k^3 \)

body.en: Two similar spheres have radii 3 and 6. Find the ratio of their volumes. \[ \text{Ratio of radii}=1:2,\quad\text{Volume ratio}=1^3:2^3=1:8. \]

Sphere: SA \(=4\pi r^2\), V \(=\tfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3\). Cylinder: SA \(=2\pi r^2+2\pi rh\), V \(=\pi r^2 h\). Cone: SA \(=\pi r^2+\pi rl\), V \(=\tfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\). For similar solids with scale factor \(k\): area scales as \(k^2\), volume scales as \(k^3\).

label.en: Worked example — Volume of composite solid

body.en:
A solid consists of a cylinder (radius 4 cm, height 6 cm) with a hemisphere on top. Find the total volume.

Cylinder: \(\pi(16)(6) = 96\pi\). Hemisphere: \(\tfrac{1}{2}\cdot\tfrac{4}{3}\pi(64) = \tfrac{128\pi}{3}\).

Total \(= 96\pi + \tfrac{128\pi}{3} = \dfrac{288\pi+128\pi}{3} = \dfrac{416\pi}{3} \approx 435.6\) cm\(^3\).

caption.en: Right circular cylinder of radius \(r = 4\) and height \(h = 10\). Volume \(V = \pi r^2 h = 160\pi\), lateral area \(L = 2\pi rh = 80\pi\), total surface area \(A = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh = 112\pi\).

label.en: ▲ EST II Math Traps & Pitfalls — 3D Solids & Similarity Ratios

body.en:
• Similar Solids Power Laws: When two solids are similar with linear scale factor \(k = L_1/L_2\): corresponding surface areas scale as \(k^2\), and volumes scale as \(k^3\). If a question states that volume increases by a factor of 8, the linear dimensions double (\(\sqrt[3]{8} = 2\)), and the surface area quadruples (\(2^2 = 4\)).
  • Cone Slant Height vs. Vertical Height: The volume formula \(V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\) requires the vertical altitude \(h\), NOT the slant height \(l\). Use the Pythagorean theorem \(r^2 + h^2 = l^2\) to solve for \(h\) before calculating volume.
  • Total Surface Area vs. Lateral Surface Area: Questions often ask for "lateral surface area" (excluding the circular base(s)) or "open cylinder" (one base). Always read carefully whether one, two, or zero circular bases are included.
  • Composite Solids Volume vs. Surface Area: While volumes of combined parts add directly (\(V_{\text{total}} = V_1 + V_2\)), surface areas do NOT add directly because the joining interface/contact face is interior and must be subtracted from both solids.

question.en: Two similar cones have surface areas in the ratio \(4:9\). If the smaller cone has volume \(16\pi\) cm\(^3\), find the volume of the larger.

solution.en: Area ratio \(= k^2 = 4/9\), so \(k = 2/3\). Volume ratio \(= k^3 = 8/27\). Larger volume \(= 16\pi \times 27/8 = 54\pi\) cm\(^3\).

question.en: A right circular cone has base radius \(r = 6\) cm and slant height \(l = 10\) cm. (a) Determine the vertical height \(h\) and volume \(V\) of the cone in terms of \(\pi\). (b) Calculate the total surface area of the cone.

solution.en:
(a) Height and Volume: The radius, vertical height, and slant height form a right triangle: \[ h = \sqrt{l^2 - r^2} = \sqrt{10^2 - 6^2} = \sqrt{100 - 36} = \sqrt{64} = 8\text{ cm}. \] The volume is: \[ V = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi (36)(8) = 96\pi\text{ cm}^3. \]

(b) Total Surface Area: Sum of base area and lateral area: \[ A = \pi r^2 + \pi r l = \pi(6^2) + \pi(6)(10) = 36\pi + 60\pi = 96\pi\text{ cm}^2. \]
